entry.title: Error Creating Content Provider for SAP Build Work Zone in Consumer Subaccount
entry.content:
I am trying to create a multi-tenant application with SAPUI5 interface that is consumed by the subscriber's SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition subscription, but I am getting errors trying to create the Content Provider. 

Following the tutorial in the documentation Developing HTML5 Business Solutions as Content Providers, which has steps for Multitenant consumption via subscription. I updated the "sap.cloud.service" in the SAPUI5 manifest.json file, added the cdm.json file and the script on the mta.yaml file to copy it to the resources folder. I also defined the destination templates in the provider side.

After that I followed the Administrator steps in Federation of HTML5 Business Solutions documentation. Subscribed to the multi-tenant app from another subaccount in the same environment and region. Exported and imported the destinations to the consumer subaccount, changing the runtime destination URL to the subscription URL of the consumer.

However after I create the Content Provider in the consumer SAP Build Work Zone channel manager, the content fetch fails with the following message:

"<Connectivity/InternalError>: Could not fetch content due to an internal error. Please try again later. If the issue persists, please open a ticket on the connectivity service."

This is the code I am currently working in https://github.tools.sap/I538205/simple-saas-mt/tree/bwz 
and I also tested the sample from https://github.com/SAP-samples/build-workzone-integration/tree/main/standard/html5-content-provider-sample which also failed to import the content provider.

Has anyone else here faced this issue? How can I solve it?

entry.title: @sap/cds-rfc: RFC_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE (NIECONN_BROKEN) in BAS using cds bind --exec, but works aft
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to run a CAP Node.js application locally in SAP Business Application Studio (BAS) using hybrid mode (cds bind --exec). The application connects to an on-premise SAP system via Destination Service + Connectivity Service + Cloud Connector using @SAP/cds-rfc.

The exact same application works perfectly when deployed to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry, but fails when run locally in BAS.

Environment

  • SAP Business Application Studio

  • Node.js: 22.13.1

  • @SAP/cds: 9.9.1

  • @SAP/cds-dk: 9.9.1

  • @SAP/cds-rfc: 2.2.1

  • @SAP-rfc/node-rfc-library: 1.1.2

  • @SAP-cloud-sdk/connectivity: 4.7.0

Hybrid setup

Service bindings are created successfully:

cds bind --to navisaccess-auth
cds bind --to navisaccess-connectivity
cds bind --to navisaccess-destination

Running:

cds bind --exec -- node rfctest.js

correctly injects all Cloud Foundry service bindings.

Minimal reproducible example

const cds = require("@sap/cds");

(async () => {
    try {
        console.log("Connecting...");

        const client = await cds.connect.to("P23_ABAP", {
            credentials: {
                destination: "P23_ABAP"
            }
        });

        console.log("Connected.");

        console.log("Calling RFC_PING...");

        const result = await client.send("RFC_PING", {});

        console.log(result);
    } catch (err) {
        console.error(err);
    }
})();

Output

Connecting...
Connected.
Calling RFC_PING...

RFCException NIECONN_BROKEN :
unable to receive data from connectivityproxy.internal.cf.ap10.hana.ondemand.com:20001

RFC_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE

Stack trace points to:

RFCService.begin()
createBapiClientConnectionHandler()
RFCClientAddonConnectionHandler.open()

What I have verified

  • cds bind works successfully.

  • Destination Service binding is successful.

  • Connectivity Service binding is successful.

  • XSUAA binding is successful.

  • cds.connect.to() succeeds.

  • The destination is resolved successfully.

  • The RFC client is created successfully.

  • The failure occurs only when the first RFC call (RFC_PING or GET_SYSTEM_TIME_REMOTE) is executed.

  • The exact same code works after deploying the application to Cloud Foundry using cf push.

  • It has has never been tested locally in BAS.

My question

Is RFC access through @SAP/cds-rfc + SAP Connectivity Service + Cloud Connector officially supported when running locally using cds bind --exec (hybrid mode)?

If yes, is there any additional configuration required for BAS or hybrid execution?

Or is RFC communication through Cloud Connector only supported for applications running inside the Cloud Foundry runtime?

Any guidance or documentation would be greatly appreciated.

entry.title: S/4HANA OData V2 Services Returning HTTP 403 – CSRF Token Validation Failed
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We are currently facing an issue while accessing S/4HANA OData V2 services from our SAP UI5 applications.

OData Services: Multiple OData V2 services in QRE
Failure Date: 28 September 2026
Approximate Time: From start of day

The applications and OData services were functioning as expected previously. However, from today, requests involving POST / $batch are consistently failing with HTTP 403 Forbidden – CSRF token validation failed.

This issue is not limited to deployment. Existing UI5 applications that were already working are also experiencing the same issue while communicating with the S/4HANA OData V2 services.

Technical Details:

The application successfully fetches the CSRF token using the X-CSRF-Token: Fetch header.

The S/4HANA backend responds successfully with HTTP 200 OK and returns an X-CSRF-Token.

The token returned by the backend is then included in the subsequent request.

However, the subsequent $batch POST request fails with HTTP 403 Forbidden – CSRF token validation failed.

Example request:

POST /sap/opu/odata/sap/<ODATA_SERVICE>/$batch

We have verified from the browser network trace that:

  1. The $batch request is nevertheless rejected with HTTP 403.

Observation:

This issue started suddenly, while the same applications and services were working previously.

The issue is also occurring with multiple existing OData V2 services/applications, so it does not appear to be specific to a particular UI5 application or a new deployment.

We would like to understand whether there have been any recent changes related to:

  • S/4HANA Gateway

  • Any recent system configuration or maintenance

Request your guidance on the possible root cause.

Screenshots of the $batch request/response

Can you please help on this issue.

Thank you.
